title: The Combination Lock
clue: Three stations, one secret order, and a vault that only opens for the right sequence.
reveal: Three stations stand in a row: a mat, a box and a towel. Only one order opens the vault, and the only hint is a happy 'yes' from you. Your dog works out the combination by trial, and gets the vault.
objective: Teach your dog by trial and error to visit three stations in a set order, ending at an opening vault.
instructions: Set three stations in a row of one room or hallway: a mat, a shallow box and a folded towel. Put the vault, a lidded box with soft treats, at the end. Non-slip floor. Pick your secret order, like box, mat, towel.
Teach the marker first: say 'yes' and hand over a treat, five times. Now 'yes' means treat is coming.
Let your dog roam. Say 'yes' and toss a treat away whenever they touch the first station in your order. Ignore other stations.
Next, mark only when they go to the second station after the first. No luring and no pointing. If they get stuck, repeat the earlier step.
When the full sequence happens, say 'yes' and open the vault. Let your dog eat from it. Keep each round to a minute or two and rest between.
Mix up the order on another day or build a longer combination. Two stations is a fine combination.
Stop if your dog looks frustrated: whining, barking or leaving. Pay the previous step, then end.
twist: Your dog has to discover the correct order of three stations, with nothing to go on but your marker, and the vault opens only when the sequence is right.
variations: Easier: two stations in a short line, one order.
Apartment: use two rooms, a mat in each.
Harder: add a fourth station or reverse the order.
Quiet dog: skip the marker and drop treats silently.
completion: Counts when your dog has done one step of the combination on their own. The vault opening is a bonus.
photoIdea: Your dog standing on the third station, with the vault box open in front of them.
memoryPrompt: What order did your dog crack first, and where did they get stuck?
dietNotes: Tiny treats from the daily ration; check labels for xylitol. Ask your vet about diet limits.
safety: Non-slip floor and plain cardboard only, no tape or plastic. Take away any box that is chewed.
Rounds last a minute or two. A frustrated dog is a stop sign, so end on a success.
One dog at a time, with no treats left on the floor between rounds.
